{{Short description|Polyhedron with 24 faces}}
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|grH}}
In [[geometry]], the '''great rhombihexacron''' (or '''great dipteral disdodecahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[great rhombihexahedron]] (U<sub>21</sub>).<ref>{{mathworld|urlname= GreatRhombihexacron|title= Great rhombihexacron}}</ref> It has 24 identical [[antiparallelogram|bow-tie]]-shaped [[Face (geometry)|faces]], 18 [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]], and 48 [[Edge (geometry)|edges]].<ref>[http://bulatov.org/polyhedra/dual/ud26.html Great Rhombihexacron]—Bulatov Abstract Creations</ref>

It has 12 outer vertices which have the same [[vertex arrangement]] as the [[cuboctahedron]], and 6 inner vertices with the vertex arrangement of an [[octahedron]].

As a surface geometry, it can be seen as visually similar to a [[Catalan solid]], the [[disdyakis dodecahedron]], with much taller rhombus-based pyramids joined to each face of a [[rhombic dodecahedron]].
== Proportions==

Each bow-tie has two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2})\approx 31.399\,714\,809\,92^{\circ}</math> and two angles of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2})\approx 62.799\,429\,619\,84^{\circ}</math>. The diagonals of each bow-tie intersect at an angle of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{2})\approx 85.800\,855\,570\,24^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-7+4\sqrt{2}}{17})\approx 94.531\,580\,798\,20^{\circ}</math>.
The ratio between the lengths of the long edges and the short ones equals <math>\sqrt{2}</math>.
